description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding N13): `wait "-1.5"` -- the TYPE-before-RANGE ordering reached through a WORD. The sibling pair `wait-negative-non-whole` / `every-negative-non-whole` pins that ordering for a number literal, but a word takes a different path: `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` coerces it first, so an implementation could order the checks correctly for numbers and range-first for words and still pass the corpus -- exactly the class the `-word` fixtures exist to close one level up (`wait-negative-word`, `wait-non-whole-word`). Found by mutation: inverting TYPE/RANGE for word arguments only left the whole corpus green. As on the plain-number arm, the correct answer is `ol-type` -- `params.actual` is `word` and `params.value` is the string the learner wrote, never the coerced `-1.5`, because the type question is settled before the range question is asked. The `primitive` event is NOT emitted, only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the argument. Its `every` twin is `every/every-negative-non-whole-word`.
